clue.text: Texan pal in a spin, left in European city

indicators.note: spinning round turns the Texan's word for a pal back to front

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend, so a Texan's pal

explanation.surface: A friend from Texas gets dizzy and is abandoned somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' turns BUD into DUB; the second 'in' simply supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland's capital is a city in Europe.

clue.text: One in state of confusion in the afternoon should swallow a drug

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the confused state, so 'in' places it within

parts.note: a daze is a muddled, stunned state
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the afternoon abbreviation encloses the article

parts.note: p.m. marks times after noon

explanation.surface: Someone muddled after lunch is told to take some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into DAZE for DIAZE, and A goes into PM for PAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam (Valium) is a sedative medicine.

clue.text: Lavish meal is not what a driver wants

definitions.meaning: slang for a huge feast where everyone overeats
a sudden tyre burst, unwelcome to any motorist

explanation.definitionFit: Both a big feed and a burst tyre go by this name, the first informally.

clue.text: US president not entirely well-liked

indicators.note: only part of the hyphenated phrase is used, so the name sits within it

explanation.surface: An American leader was only moderately popular.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'well-liked'; Eisenhower's slogan was 'I like Ike', which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, the 34th American head of state.

clue.text: Sayings from the last two thousand years

parts.note: AD, anno domini, labels the roughly two millennia of the common era
ages means a very long time, many years

explanation.surface: Proverbs that have been handed down since Roman times.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs and maxims are old sayings passed down by tradition.

clue.text: Release John Boorman movie

definitions.meaning: the 1972 backwoods thriller directed by Boorman

explanation.definitionFit: The word means rescue from bondage, and it is also the title of Boorman's canoe-trip film.

clue.text: Cooper managed to enter store

indicators.note: one piece enters the film star's first name and sits inside it

parts.note: Gary Cooper was a Hollywood star
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A man named Cooper succeeded in getting into a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for grain.

clue.text: Disorganised group demonstration in front of the Queen

indicators.note: one piece is placed before the royal abbreviation

parts.note: a show is a display or demonstration
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A ragtag bunch put on a display for Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'shower' is a useless, chaotic lot.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a hopeless, incompetent bunch of people a shower.

clue.text: Lady one's noticed loitering in pubs

indicators.note: someone seen hanging about inside the pubs, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bars are pubs or drinking places
one's gives the letters of one plus S

explanation.surface: A titled woman has been spotted hanging around drinking establishments.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a noblewoman, so addressed as Lady.

clue.text: Wild cat spared no fluttering bird in its clutches

indicators.note: the rearranged phrase holds the bird inside it
fluttering suggests things flapping about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A big cat let a flapping bird go free while holding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges SPARED NO into SNEOPARD, and 'in its clutches' puts OWL inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is a big wild cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Fool teacher taken on by local education authority

indicators.note: the teacher is added after the authority, joining it

parts.note: LEA is the abbreviation for a local education authority
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A council hires a silly teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: An LEA was the British council body running state schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive or string them along.

clue.text: Fellow, one bitten by big bird, is very brave

parts.note: he stands for a male person, a fellow

indicators.note: being bitten puts one piece in the bird's mouth, inside it

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man who gets pecked by a huge bird is remarkably courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic means displaying courage like a hero.

clue.text: Likely characters in Animal Farm, such a ridiculous kind of story

definitions.meaning: a rooster and a male bovine are plausible farmyard creatures in Orwell's novel

definitions.text: such a ridiculous kind of story

explanation.definitionFit: A tall, unbelievable tale is called a cock-and-bull story, and the two male animals would fit on Orwell's farm.

clue.text: Forestalls old boy, determined to reverse onto Roman road

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
via is Latin for road

indicators.note: reversing makes the word for determined run backwards

parts.note: set means determined or fixed

explanation.surface: A former pupil is resolved to back his car onto an ancient highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns SET into TES, which goes onto the end of VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate is to prevent or anticipate a problem, so to forestall it.

clue.text: Very much how fastidious people behave?

definitions.meaning: fussy people act in a choosy, exacting way

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means especially, and also in a fussy, choosy manner, from the adjective for fastidious.

clue.text: Reportedly bad state of ships

indicators.note: reported speech means we go by what is said, the sound of the words

parts.note: naughty means bad or misbehaving; Cal is short for California, an American state

explanation.surface: We hear that some state is in a poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to sailors, the sea and shipping.

clue.text: Noel adored, surprisingly, by almost everyone in this TV show

indicators.note: a surprising turn implies the letters come out unexpectedly rearranged
almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: The presenter Noel is, unexpectedly, loved by nearly all viewers of his programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges NOEL ADORED into DEALORNODE; 'almost' drops the last letter of ALL to give AL. Noel Edmonds hosted the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The game show hosted by Noel Edmonds on Channel 4 had contestants choosing boxes.

clue.text: Gather information from French lawyer

parts.note: de is the French word for from
brief is British slang for a barrister or lawyer

explanation.surface: Collect facts from a Parisian solicitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link but, with 'French', gives DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them after a mission to collect details.

clue.text: Relaxation? Inside tent expect a certain amount

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a portion of them

explanation.surface: A camper anticipates a little rest inside the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like the container signal, but its last two letters start the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of tension between states, a relaxing of hostilities.

clue.text: Repair broken weapon

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fix a damaged sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a thin, sharp-pointed sword.

clue.text: Federal agents arresting American chap in distant land

indicators.note: arresting someone holds them in, so the agency encloses the other pieces

parts.note: the CIA is a US federal intelligence agency
bod is British slang for a person or chap

explanation.surface: US government agents detain a man from America in a far-off country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in South-East Asia, far from Britain.

clue.text: English country property

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A rural mansion in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is landed property, often a large house with grounds.

clue.text: Setting fresh limit finally rejected by European Union

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new order
the final letter of the word is thrown out

explanation.surface: Brussels turns down a new cap on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally rejected' takes the T off LIMIT, and 'fresh' rearranges LIMI into MILI.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a social environment or surroundings.

clue.text: Fellow parking small car in port area

indicators.note: the car is put in the harbour area, inside it

parts.note: a dock is part of a port
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A man leaves his little car at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' is the definition, a man's name; 'parking' only dresses the scene, while 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominick is a man's name, so a fellow.

clue.text: Shortly identify damage

indicators.note: being cut short loses the word's final letter

parts.note: to mark something is to identify it

explanation.surface: In brief, spot the harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or damage.

clue.text: Regulation to suppress very loud drumbeat

indicators.note: suppressing holds something down within, so the musical mark is enclosed

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A rule is brought in to quieten a noisy drumming.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffle is a low, continuous drum roll.

clue.text: Even parts of 16 can be a distressing experience

parts.note: the TV show's title contains the word for an alternative
the same title also contains the word for a bargain

explanation.surface: Even bits of the game show can be traumatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is DEAL OR NO DEAL; two of its words, OR and DEAL, joined give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or harrowing trial.
